Container.Name: spin-dashboard
Container.Overview: Shows when your hard drives spin up and down, and why. A timeline per disk with every spin-up, the file that woke the drive, and which process opened it: a Docker container (Plex, Sonarr, Bazarr, ...), Unraid itself (mover, cron, webGUI) or a user (SMB share, shell). Works with the array and with HDD pools (XFS, Btrfs, ZFS).[br][br] How it works: drive state is polled with hdparm -C, which never wakes a sleeping drive. File access is traced with fanotify (fatrace). Because of that the container needs privileged mode, the host PID namespace, read-only access to /mnt and the Docker socket (to show container names). It never writes to your shares.[br][br] Tip: keep the appdata path on an SSD/cache pool, otherwise the dashboard itself keeps a drive awake.
Container.Requires: Run on Unraid 6.12 or newer. Requires privileged mode and --pid=host (set in Extra Parameters).

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: Where spin.csv, disks.csv and who.csv are stored. Keep this on an SSD/cache pool.

Config.Name: Mounts (read-only)
Config.Description: Read-only access to the array and pools, needed to trace which files are opened. Slave propagation picks up pools that mount after the container started.

Config.Name: Unraid disk info (read-only)
Config.Description: Unraid's disk state (disks.ini), used for names like parity, disk1 and pool members.

Config.Name: Docker socket (read-only)
Config.Description: Only used to look up container names for the processes that open files.

Config.Name: Retention (days)
Config.Description: How many days of history to keep.

Config.Name: Watch override
Config.Description: Optional, space separated. Leave empty to watch all HDD-backed disks and pools automatically, e.g. /mnt/disk1 /mnt/tank

Config.Name: Ignore processes
Config.Description: Space separated process names whose file access is not logged, including their child processes. Default skips the Cache Dirs plugin, which constantly scans all folders.
